26.title: The Appearance of Melchizedek and His Influence on Eastern and Western Religions
26.001.h3: 1. Identity of Melchizedek and the Circumstances of His Coming to Urantia
26.003.p: Melchizedeks are an emergency order of sons who appear throughout the local universe whenever unusual conditions arise or extraordinary tasks must be accomplished, and Machiventa Melchizedek was one of the twelve Melchizedeks who assumed custody of Urantia immediately after the Caligastia betrayal and who retained administrative authority until the time of Adam and Eve, remaining as planetary receivers until the Creator Son Jesus became the nominal Planetary Prince of Urantia [93:0.1]–0.2.
26.004.h4: 2) Time and reason for his arrival
26.005.p: After the failure of Adam, revealed truth on Urantia was nearly extinguished, and around 3000 B.C. the idea of God had faded to a faint remnant in the human mind, making an emergency measure necessary to preserve spiritual light, whereupon Machiventa Melchizedek volunteered to incarnate as a temporary human being, an act performed only six times in the entire history of Nebadon, and he appeared on Urantia exactly 1,973 years before the birth of Jesus [93:1.1]–1.3; 93:2.1.
26.006.h4: 3) Nature of his incarnation and length of service
26.007.p: Melchizedek materialized near what would become Salem in Palestine, appearing in a special physical form resembling a human male though derived from no human stock, and he lived on Earth for ninety-four years without marriage or offspring, first being seen by the shepherd Amdon while wearing upon his chest the emblem of three concentric circles signifying Paradise Trinity sovereignty [93:2.1]–2.6.
26.009.p: He introduced himself as “Melchizedek, priest of El Elyon, the Most High, the one universal God,” while his three concentric circles were commonly interpreted by the people of that time as representing the three kingdoms of man, angels, and God [93:2.1]; 93:3.3.
26.010.h3: 2. Major Teachings and Mission Objectives of Machiventa Melchizedek
26.012.p: Melchizedek proclaimed the existence of a single, universal God and subordinated every other concept to this supreme doctrine, deliberately preparing the world for the later bestowal of Michael of Nebadon (Jesus), who would reveal this same Universal Father to all humanity [93:3.2]–3.6.
26.014.p: Melchizedek’s covenant with Abraham embodied the great Urantian agreement between divinity and humanity by teaching that salvation does not come through ritual offerings but solely through personal faith in God and trust in His promises, thus restoring to the world the truth that grace is obtained through belief rather than sacrifice [93:6.3]–6.4.
26.015.h4: 3) The Salem creed and the seven commandments
26.016.p: The Salem believers accepted three central articles of faith: belief in El Elyon as the sole universal Father and Creator, belief that God grants favor on the basis of faith rather than sacrifice, and commitment to obey Melchizedek’s seven commandments while spreading his gospel, including the primary injunction to worship no god other than the Creator of heaven and earth and to doubt not that faith is the only requirement for eternal survival [93:4.2]–4.8.
26.017.h4: 4) Replacement of sacrifices with the communion service
26.018.p: Melchizedek abolished ancient blood-sacrifice customs by instituting the simple symbols of bread and wine, a practice that later profoundly influenced the Christian sacrament of communion [93:4.14].
26.019.h3: 3. Relationship with Abraham and the Broader Influence on World Religions
26.021.p: Abraham wholeheartedly accepted Melchizedek’s teaching, becoming his foremost disciple and supporter, voluntarily giving one-tenth of his war spoils to Salem after the battle of Siddim, while Melchizedek redirected Abraham from worldly conquest toward the spiritual vision of the heavenly kingdom, charging him to preserve the truth of monotheism for future generations [93:4.16]; 93:5.13; 93:6..
26.022.h4: 2) Spread of Salem missionaries across East and West
26.023.p: The Salem teachers carried Melchizedek’s gospel to Egypt, Mesopotamia, Asia Minor, throughout Europe as far as the British Isles, and even across Asia to China and Japan, though by the time of Jesus much of their teaching had been absorbed, altered, or overshadowed by older evolutionary beliefs and local superstitions, a universal pattern in which every new revelation becomes contaminated by existing religious traditions [93:7.1]–7.4.
26.025.p: As people—including his own associates—began to venerate Melchizedek excessively as a supernatural being, he withdrew from Earth quietly one night, and later Hebrew scholars, finding early records too extraordinary, preserved only the account of Abraham meeting Melchizedek after the battle of Siddim while discarding most other narratives, resulting in the tragic loss of teachings that would have prepared the Jews to recognize the mission of the coming Creator Son, Michael, when he appeared in the flesh centuries later [93:8.1]; 93:9.6–9.10.
26.026.h3: 4. Present Status and Continuing Function of Melchizedek
26.027.h4: 1) His role among the twenty-four counselors
26.028.p: Following Jesus’ triumph and his designation as Planetary Prince of Urantia, Machiventa Melchizedek became one of the twenty-four counselors stationed on Jerusem devoted to Urantia’s affairs, and he now serves as the personal ambassador of the Creator Son while holding the title of Vicegerent Planetary Prince, strongly implying that he will permanently replace the deposed Caligastia as the rightful guardian of the planet [93:10.5]–10..
27.title: The Nature of Religion, Religious Experience, and the Foundations of Faith
27.001.h3: 1. The Nature of Religion and Its Dynamic Definition
27.002.h4: 1) The definition and characteristics of religion
27.003.p: Religion is a dynamic life experience that transforms an ordinary individual into a personality endowed with idealistic power [100:0.1]. Spiritual growth is fostered through intimate and stimulating relationships with fellow believers [100:0.2]. Religion is not a technique for achieving static peace of mind but an impulse that organizes the soul for dynamic service [100:3.1]. True religion is the experience of divinity in the consciousness of a moral creature, enabling spiritual satisfaction while still in the flesh and allowing the soul to experience eternal realities within time [101:1.1]. Religion ranges from primitive fear to the noble freedom of a civilized mortal who realizes his sonship with the eternal God [101:0.1]. It operates beyond reason and logic, functioning through trust, faith, and assurance [101:0.3].
27.004.h4: 2) The value and influence of religion
27.005.p: All genuine religion centers on unwavering loyalty to the highest values and wholehearted devotion to supreme goals [100:3.1]. Such devotion inspires the believer to pay any price required to attain the eternal reward. Furthermore, true religion is living love expressed through a life of service, ennobling even the ordinary and demanding tasks of daily living [100:6.5], 100:0.2. Religion elevates human existence and becomes the most powerful source of inner growth.
27.006.h3: 2. Conditions of Personal Spiritual Growth and Problems of Development
27.007.h4: 1) The nature and conditions of growth
27.008.p: Spiritual growth results in the expansion of meanings and the enhancement of values, while evil arises when personal judgments are mistakenly elevated to absolute levels [100:1.1]. The measure of growth lies not in results but in progress itself [100:1.3]. Although the factors of growth may be intentional, actual growth is always unconscious in its unfolding [100:1.7]~8. The essential soil for spiritual growth includes progressive self-realization, harmony of inherent tendencies, a willingness to adventure, and humility balanced with confidence [100:1.5]. The main obstacles to growth are prejudice and ignorance [100:1.2].
27.009.h4: 2) Spiritual development and its inner processes
27.010.p: True educational growth appears as the elevation of ideals, the expansion of value standards, the emergence of new meanings, and the strengthening of loyalty to supreme values [100:1.3]. Spiritual development depends on maintaining a living connection with true spiritual forces and consistently sharing spiritual fruits with one’s fellows [100:2.1]. Religious living is creative, original, and devoted [100:4.1]. No growth occurs without mental conflict or spiritual agitation, and new meanings are always born from such struggles [100:4.1], 100:4.2.
27.011.h3: 3. The Deepening of Faith and the Altruistic Experience
27.012.h4: 1) The enrichment of meanings and values
27.013.p: The highest goal of human life is the growth of meanings, the expansion of values, and the realization of their universal interrelatedness—a state equivalent to God-consciousness [100:3.6]. Experience enhances meanings, and values become real when spiritually related to living realities [100:3.4]. Spiritual growth leads to joy that surpasses all understanding and to a peace that withstands every disappointment [100:4.3], 100:6.6.
27.015.p: To love one’s fellows is to discover their inherent value [100:4.4]. Love is born from a thorough understanding of another’s motives and emotions [100:4.6]. Genuine understanding produces tolerance, tolerance grows into friendship, and friendship matures into love [100:4.4]. Awareness of God may arise gradually or appear suddenly during a crisis [100:5.3]. Yet mysticism must not become an escape technique, and ecstasy should never be mistaken for genuine religious experience [100:5.8]. Morontia access to Adjuster contact becomes clearer through living faith, sincere worship, and unselfish prayer [100:5.7], 102:4.5. Jesus never used mystical techniques to commune with the Father [100:5.11], and the unique feature of his personality was its symmetry and balanced unity rather than mere perfection [100:7.1]. Jesus trusted the heavenly Father as earthly children trust their parents [100:7.7], and his most original teaching was the emphasis on love and mercy instead of fear and sacrifice [100:7.5].
27.016.h3: 4. The Foundations of Deity and the Certainty of Spiritual Reality
27.018.p: Religion ultimately leads to the consciousness of God and to the firm assurance of the survival of the faithful personality [101:1.6]. The realization of spiritual values is called God-consciousness [103:1.6]. This awareness becomes possible through the indwelling Thought Adjuster, the Paradise Father’s personal gift to humankind [103:0.1]. The Adjuster is the universe window through which finite creatures can glimpse the certainty and divinity of the Infinite Father by faith [103:0.1].
27.019.h4: 2) The reality of Deity and the experiential certainty of faith
27.020.p: God is too absolute to be demonstrated by material evidence; He is known only through faith, and this faith depends entirely on personal participation in His divine reality [102:1.5]. Religious experience requires God to be a personality [102:7.3], for a non-personal God could never be part of authentic human religious experience. The soul that knows God dares to proclaim, “I know,” because God is the supreme certainty of all religious experience [102:6.5], 102:6.4. The divine spirit contacts mortals not through emotion but through the highest realms of spiritually uplifted thinking [101:1.3]. True divinity can be discovered only through religious experience and the living practice of genuine faith [101:10.15].
27.021.h3: 5. Knowledge, Faith, and the Cosmic Outlook
27.022.h4: 1) The relationship of faith, knowledge, and understanding
27.023.p: Belief may be limiting and collective, but faith is expanding, liberating, and personal [101:8.2]. Faith is a living experience that deals with spiritual meanings, divine ideals, and supreme values [101:8.2]. Science deals with facts and uses the method of reason to produce knowledge, while religion deals with values and uses the method of faith to yield happiness [101:5.2] Philosophy seeks to unify facts and values, producing harmony and coherence [101:5.2].
27.025.p: Revelation supplements the absence of the morontia viewpoint and confirms the harmonious integration of science, philosophy, and religion [101:2.8], 101:2.2. Morontia mota is a technique of higher comprehension, a supra-philosophic reconciliation that removes all differences between reason and faith [103:6.7]. Religion should not be organically involved in social reconstruction or economic reorganization [99:1.6], but it must provide moral stability and promote spiritual growth amid constant change [99:1.2]. True religion creates in the individual a cosmic loyalty that leads to successful social service [99:3.16]. The faith of Jesus revealed the path to humanity’s ultimate salvation and cosmic attainment [101:6.8]: liberation from material bondage through the realization of sonship with God, liberation from intellectual bondage through the truth [101:6.9], 101:6.10, and finally the achievement of eternal life through complete union with divinity in the Supreme [101:6.14], 101:6.15.
28.title: The World Religion
28.003.p: The doctrine of Cynicism preserved more of the teachings of the Melchizedek disciples than any other religion except Judaism [131:1.1]. Cynics recognized God as the Most High, the supreme being of heaven and earth, the perfect circle of eternity, and the only creator who rules the universe of universes [131:1.2]. This God is immortal, infinite, omnipotent, and all-bountiful, granting peace and faithfully protecting all who fear and trust Him [131:1.3], 131:1.4.
28.005.p: They taught that humans gain knowledge from experience but acquire wisdom by contemplating the Most High [131:1.4]. Since all creatures live in the Creator and He indwells His creatures, one must seek Him within the mind [131:1.5]. The God-knowing person regards all men as brothers [131:1.6] and conquers evil with good, refusing to do to others what he would not wish done to himself [131:1.7].
28.008.p: The preserved and revised records of the Palestinian Kenites contained much of Melchizedek's teachings [131:2.1]. Judaism taught that in the beginning God created the heavens and the earth and that there is no other beside Him, commanding humans to love the Lord with all their heart, soul, and strength [131:2.2]. God is merciful, gracious, long-suffering, abundant in goodness and truth [131:2.3], the healer of the brokenhearted, and a refuge and strength to His people [131:2.4].
28.010.p: Those who wait upon the Lord will renew their strength [131:2.6], and God will judge every deed, both good and evil, even the secret things [131:2.8]. Judaism emphasized loving one’s neighbor as oneself, bearing no grudges [131:2.11], and fulfilling one’s whole duty by keeping the commandments—loving God, honoring parents, and refraining from murder, adultery, theft, false witness, and covetousness [131:2.12], 131:2.7.
28.013.p: Ganid marveled that Buddhism approached a religion without a personal and universal God, yet early Buddhism reflected the influence of Melchizedek missionaries in India [131:3.1]. Buddhism taught that righteousness and true humanness are grasped by faith, that justice and mercy are cultivated by meditation [131:3.2], and that happiness and peace come from pure thoughts and virtuous living [131:3.3], 131:3.5.
28.015.p: The one who attains assurance of salvation is free from lust, envy, and hatred [131:3.4] and must patiently work for his own deliverance [131:3.4]. The golden rule was expressed as refraining from doing to others what one would not desire for oneself [131:3.6]. The altruistic soul, they taught, will ascend to Paradise and enjoy the happiness of infinite liberty [131:3.7].
28.018.p: Later Hinduism blended the monotheistic teachings carried by the Melchizedek missionaries with earlier concepts [131:4.1], 131:4.2. God was viewed as the Supreme in every respect, the creator and controller of the universe of universes [131:4.2]. “I dwell within them as the light of wisdom,” the Lord is quoted as saying [131:4.3].
28.020.p: The primal spirit of God dwells within the human soul, serving as the eternal witness of virtue and evil within the mind [131:4.3]. Moral duty is summarized as refraining from doing to others what one finds repugnant to oneself and conquering anger and hatred with compassion [131:4.6]. To know God is to break the bonds of death, escape the illusion of evil, and attain final liberation [131:4.7].
28.023.p: Except for Judaism, Zoroastrianism preserved more of the Salem teachings than any other religion, and Zoroaster had direct contact with descendants of early Melchizedek missionaries [131:5.1]. They taught that everything good, wise, and righteous comes from the one all-knowing God, the source of all light [131:5.2]. God is the source of our wisdom, life, soul, and bodily vitality [131:5.3].
28.025.p: They held that true wisdom consists in acting in harmony with the spirit of truth [131:5.2]. Whether a wrong is intentional or accidental, repentance removes its stain from the soul [131:5.5]. God promises immortality to the devout soul that thinks purely and acts righteously [131:5.2].
28.028.p: This group preserved the Melchizedek doctrine of the One God and is now associated with the followers of Jainism [131:6.1]. They believed that the sinner would fail to ascend while the righteous would find a dwelling place in heaven [131:6.2].
28.030.p: They taught that the greatest enemy of the human soul is the self and that the greatest victory is self-conquest [131:6.2]. They insisted that one should treat all fellow creatures as one wishes to be treated while traveling through life [131:6.2].
28.033.p: A manuscript recently added to the Alexandrian library revealed this Far Eastern religion, containing remnants of early Melchizedek teachings [131:7.1]. The Lord declared, “⟦Q 131:7.2⟧You are all recipients of my divine power⟦/Q⟧” [131:7.2]. The King of Heaven seeks to reveal Himself through both the beauty of nature and the virtues of humanity [131:7.2].
28.035.p: Shinto taught that pride conceals God and must be abandoned to receive heavenly help [131:7.3]. God hears the prayers of those with clean hearts free from deceit and hypocrisy [131:7.3].
28.038.p: The monotheistic teachings carried by Melchizedek messengers into China found expression in several Chinese religions, with Taoism preserving them most consistently [131:8.1]. The Supreme is pure and serene, the glorious ancestor of all things, and the mother of the world [131:8.2], 131:8.4. Knowledge of the Eternal brings enlightenment and wisdom, while ignorance of Him results in evil and sin [131:8.2].
28.040.p: True goodness is like water—blessing all and harming none [131:8.3]. They taught that kindness should answer injury and that all people should be loved [131:8.4]. Above all, one must remember that God rewards people for what they are rather than for what they do [131:8.5].
28.043.p: Although Confucianism recognized God less than any major world religion, it still acknowledged the monotheistic doctrine of the Melchizedek missionaries [131:9.1]. Heaven’s decrees are perfect, and mercy is Heaven’s greatest gift to humanity; therefore, Heaven may be called both Father and Mother [131:9.2].
28.045.p: Confucianism taught that the human goal is to attain the perfection of Paradise [131:9.4]. It also expressed the golden rule: Do not do to others what you would not have them do to you [131:9.4]. It regarded the practice of mercy in all judgment as the way of Heaven [131:9.4].
28.048.p: Ganid summarized his personal faith, shaped through Jesus’s teachings, and called it “Our Religion” [131:10.1]. He affirmed that the Lord our God is one and that humans must love Him with all their heart and mind while loving all His children as themselves [131:10.2]. He believed God cannot be found through mere knowledge but must be known through personal experience within the heart [131:10.3].
28.050.p: Ganid declared that the heavenly Father loves even the wicked and is kind to the unthankful [131:10.4]. He resolved to worship God by treating every human being as he believed God wishes to treat His children [131:10.5] and adopted the golden rule as his own living faith: Do to others as you would have them do to you [131:10.7]. He realized that no one could rejoice in the Fatherhood of God without accepting the brotherhood of all men [131:10.7].
28.052.p: Ganid concluded that although he found traces of God in all other religions, the God of “Our Religion” was more beautiful, loving, merciful, personal, and above all, his own spiritual Father, and he recognized himself as God’s child [131:10.8]. In this discovery he found the religion of eternal salvation [131:10.8].
28.053.p: These ten religious traditions reveal a common thread: monotheism and the universal golden rule, proving the consistent spiritual truth spread worldwide through ancient Melchizedek missions [131:0.1].
29.title: The Evolution of Yahweh: From Tribal God to Universal Father
29.001.h3: 1. The Primitive Concept of Yahweh among Early Semitic Tribes
29.003.p: Early Semitic tribes believed in various spirits dwelling in everything, such as the spirits of plants, animals, fire, water, and air, which were objects of fear and worship [96:1.1]. Yahweh originated as one of these spirits, specifically a tribal god of Southern Palestine associated with Mount Horeb, the Sinai volcano [96:1.3]. Until about 2000 B.C., Mount Sinai experienced intermittent volcanic activity, and the associated fire, smoke, and thunder greatly impacted the surrounding Bedouins, causing them to fear Yahweh greatly [96:1.11], 96:4.5. This spirit of Horeb eventually became the god of the Hebrew Semites, whom they eventually believed surpassed all other gods [96:1.11]. Early Hebrews were taught to regard Yahweh as "the Almighty; the Lord is a man of war, a God of battle," reflecting a concept that was primitive, crude, and human-centered [96:5.7], 96:5.8. This early Yahweh was often symbolized by the golden calf [96:5.8].
29.005.p: Hebrew religion was founded upon the covenant between Abraham and Machiventa Melchizedek [96:0.3]. The teachings of Melchizedek concerning 'El Elyon' (the Most High God of heaven) influenced the Hebrew faith [96:1.4]. Moses' father-in-law was a Kenite who worshiped El Elyon [96:4.2]. During their enslavement in Egypt, the lower-class Hebrew slaves maintained their traditional belief in Yahweh as a race god [96:2.4], 96:2.5. The concept of El Shaddai, derived from Amenemope’s wisdom and influenced by Akhenaton's Aton teachings and Melchizedek's El Elyon, also permeated the Hebrew mind, though it became thoroughly colored by the desert Yahweh faith [96:1.5].
29.006.h3: 2. Elevation to a National God by Moses
29.007.h4: 1) Moses' Reconstitution of the Divine Concept
29.008.p: Moses, an extraordinary leader and organizer, combined the traditions of the Melchizedek era with Egyptian knowledge to create an improved religion for the Israelites [96:5.1], 96:5.3, 96:15.3. Following the exodus from Egypt, when the Hebrews encamped around Mount Sinai, Moses decided wisely to proclaim a new, expanded concept of Deity, derived from his own earlier beliefs, as an enlarged concept of their old tribal god, Yahweh [96:4.2]. He proclaimed Yahweh as the Lord God of Israel, firmly establishing that Yahweh was above all gods and supreme to the Hebrews [96:4.3], 96:4.6.
29.010.p: Moses made heroic efforts to elevate Yahweh to the Supreme God, presenting him as "the God of truth, a God without iniquity, righteous and upright in all his ways" [96:4.7]. Despite these efforts, the limited comprehension of his followers forced him to speak of a God described in human form, one who was easily influenced by human actions and capable of anger and wrath [96:4.7]. He taught that Yahweh was a "jealous God" and an austere master [96:4.6]. Moses tried to expand their concept, however, by teaching that Yahweh was also the "God of the spirits of all flesh" and that "the eternal God is your refuge, and underneath are the everlasting arms" [96:4.6]. Nevertheless, upon Moses’ death, the concept of Yahweh quickly relapsed into the semi-barbaric ideas of the old Horeb and desert gods [96:5.8].
29.011.h3: 3. Evolution toward Universalism through the Prophets
29.012.h4: 1) Samuel and the Doctrine of Immutability
29.013.p: After Moses, the Yahweh concept rapidly deteriorated [96:6.1]. Samuel, born into a lineage of Salem teachers who sought to maintain Melchizedek's truths, worked to restore the worship of the Supreme Yahweh [97:1.2]. Samuel’s greatest contribution to the evolution of the God concept was his resounding declaration that Yahweh was unchanging and always embodied the same errorless perfection and divinity [97:1.4]. He proclaimed the stability in the relationship with Deity, stating: "The strength of Israel will not lie nor repent, for he is not a man that he should repent" [97:1.4], 97:1.5. This marked the beginning of the rise of Yahweh from a tribal god ideal to the powerful, unchanging Creator and Supervisor of all creation [97:1.4].
29.014.h4: 2) Elijah and the Defeat of Baal
29.015.p: The long controversy between Yahweh loyalists and Baal devotees was primarily a socio-economic clash of ideologies regarding land tenure (Yahweh loyalists believed land was inalienable from the tribe, given by God [97:3.2]; Baal worshipers believed land could be freely bought and sold [97:3.3]). Elijah, however, converted this struggle into a religious issue between the Hebrews and the Canaanites [97:3.1], 97:3.6. Since there were many Baals but only one Yahweh, the victory in this dispute led to the defeat of polytheism by monotheism [97:3.5].
29.016.h4: 3) The Dawn of Justice and Mercy (Amos and Hosea)
29.017.p: Amos arrived in the eighth century B.C. and boldly attacked the belief that Yahweh would condone sin among the supposedly 'chosen people' [97:4.2]. Amos was not merely a reformer but a discoverer of a new concept of God [97:4.2]. He proclaimed Yahweh as the God of all nations and asserted that God would not hold Israel's crimes and sins differently from those of other peoples [97:4.2], 97:4.4. Amos sought to portray the unyielding justice of Yahweh [97:4.3]. Following Amos, Hosea took up the doctrine of a just universal God and revived Moses' concept of a God of love [97:4.5]. Hosea preached forgiveness through repentance, not sacrifice, presenting Yahweh as a God of mercy and love [97:4.5], 97:4.6.
29.019.p: The First Isaiah preached the eternal nature, infinite wisdom, and unchanging reliability of God [97:5.2]. His message of forgiveness—"Come now, and let us reason together; though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool"—brought great solace to the fear-ridden Hebrews [97:5.2].
29.021.p: Jeremiah marked the next bold step in expanding the Yahweh concept internationally [97:6.1]. He fearlessly declared that Yahweh would not take the side of the Hebrews in their military conflicts with other nations [97:6.2]. Jeremiah asserted that Yahweh was the God of all lands and all peoples, culminating the internationalization of the Hebrew God and declaring, "Yes, I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore with loving-kindness have I drawn you" [97:6.2], 97:6.3.
29.022.h3: 4. Climax into the Universal God Concept (Second Isaiah)
29.024.p: During the Babylonian captivity, the teachings of the Second Isaiah elevated the Yahweh concept to its sublime apex, finally establishing the idea of the Universal God [97:7.1], 97:7.4. Second Isaiah fully embraced the God of justice, love, and mercy of the First Isaiah, and preached Yahweh as the Creator and Preserver of the universe [97:7.6]. He deliberately transcended anthropomorphism, proclaiming: "Behold, he taketh up the isles as a very little thing" and "I am the first and the last; and besides me there is no God" [97:7.6]. This great Hebrew thinker thoroughly demolished the concept of a national God [97:7.11].
29.026.p: Second Isaiah presented Yahweh as the tender Father of all mankind, emphasizing infinite attributes and unconditional love [97:7.13]. His comforting message to the exiles included: "Can a woman forget her nursing infant, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb? Yes, they may forget, yet will I not forget you. Behold, I have graven you upon the palms of my hands" [97:7.7]. He proclaimed salvation through grace and forgiveness, saying: "Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts; and let him return to the Lord, and he will have mercy upon him, and to our God, for he will abundantly pardon" [97:7.7].
29.028.p: The God concept preached by the Second Isaiah was unmatched by any prophet or religious teacher from Melchizedek's time up to the era of Jesus [97:7.4], 97:7.5. This concept became the highest Western concept of God, embracing cosmic justice, divine mercy, and eternal righteousness [97:7.13]. It represented the highest human visualization of the Universal Father until it was further amplified and refined by the personal teachings and life example of Michael of Nebadon (Jesus) [97:10.8]. The old, cruel, and jealous concept of Yahweh, the desert god of the Bedouins, had all but perished, replaced by the brilliant proclamation of the divinity of the Universal Father [97:7.11], 97:10.8.
30.title: The Development of Modern Civilization and Evolution of Marriage
30.001.h3: 1. Major Facts on the Development of Modern Civilization
30.002.h4: 1) The Cradle of Civilization and Evolutionary Compulsion
30.003.p: Despite the failure of the world improvement plan set forth in the missions of Caligastia and Adam, the basic organic evolution of the human race advanced the race in the measure of human progress and racial development, for evolution may be delayed but cannot be stopped [81:0.1]. Though fewer in numbers than planned, the influence of the violet race brought about advances in civilization since the days of Adam exceeding the whole of human previous existence covering almost one million years [81:0.2]. For about 35,000 years after the days of Adam, the cradle of civilization was situated in southwestern Asia, extending from the Nile Valley eastward, slightly northward across northern Arabia to Mesopotamia, and up into Turkestan [81:1.1]. Great climatic and geologic changes in northern Africa and western Asia terminated the early Adamite migrations, diverted migration streams north and east into Turkestan [81:1.2], and now climatic evolution is forcing the Eurasian peoples to abandon hunting and take up the higher vocations of pasturage and agriculture [81:1.3].
30.004.p: Man generally evolved from hunter through the pastoral age to the farmer, and this was also true of the Andites [81:1.5], but more frequently, the evolutionary compulsion of climatic necessity brought about the direct transition of whole tribes from hunters to successful farmers, occurring only in regions having a high admixture of the violet race strain [81:1.5]. All throughout southwestern Asia, in the fertile river bottoms and adjacent plains, the Andites were practicing improved agricultural techniques inherited from their ancestors, whose chief vocations within the borders of the second garden were agriculture and horticulture [81:1.6].
30.005.h4: 2) Four Major Tools of Civilizational Advancement
30.006.p: The growth of culture depended upon the development of the tools of civilization, and the devices used by man as he emerged from savagery were effective when they released human power for the performance of higher tasks [81:2.1]. The first four great advances of human civilization were: the harnessing of fire [81:2.4], the domestication of animals [81:2.5], the enslavement of captives [81:2.6], and private property [81:2.7]. Fire was the first great discovery, but it was of little value to primitive man because he failed to recognize natural causation and persisted in adhering to supernatural explanations [81:2.8].
30.007.p: In the prescientific age, the only way man could accomplish work without doing it himself was by using animals [81:2.10], and the domestication of animals opened the way for agriculture and transportation, without which man could not have emerged from primitive status to subsequent civilization phases [81:2.10]. Most of the animals suited for domestication were found in central and southwestern Asia, which is one reason why civilization advanced more rapidly in that region than elsewhere [81:2.11]. With agriculture came the introduction of slavery and private land ownership [81:2.13], and slavery elevated the living standard of the master and provided more leisure for social culture [81:2.13].
30.008.h4: 3) Growth of Cities, Manufacturing, and Commerce
30.009.p: Beginning about 12,000 B.C., as the lush grass hunting and grazing grounds of Turkestan were destroyed by climatic changes, the inhabitants of that region were compelled to resort to new forms of industry and early manufacturing, and those with higher Andite intelligence chose to engage in trade and manufacturing [81:3.1]. The increase in trade and manufacturing (processing raw materials into diverse commercial products) directly resulted in the formation of early semi-peaceful communities, which played a very important role in disseminating the culture of civilization and the arts [81:3.2]. Trade contributed to the more rapid cross-fertilization of culture by bringing diverse kinds of human beings into communication [81:3.2], and about twelve thousand years ago, the era of independent cities was just opening, and these early trade and manufacturing cities were always surrounded by areas for agriculture and pasturage [81:3.3].
30.010.p: The widespread use of metal characterized the era of early industrial and trade cities [81:3.4], bronze culture was discovered in Turkestan even before 9000 B.C., and the Andites early learned to work iron, gold, and copper [81:3.4], 81:3.5, 81:3.4. Trade became the most potent influence in spreading cultural civilization [81:3.6], and traveling merchants and wandering explorers contributed more to the advancement of historic civilization than military conquest, colonization, or later missionary activities combined [81:3.7].
30.011.h4: 4) Maintenance and Essential Elements of Civilization
30.012.p: Cultural civilization does not thrive without a proper background of antecedent racial evolution [81:5.1], but the Adamite blood strain augmented the inherent capacity of the races and quickened the pace of economic and industrial development [81:5.1]. Among the factors influencing the maintenance of civilization, the natural environment (climate and physical conditions) determines the character and scope of material civilization [81:6.3]. Cultural civilization arises only in conditions of material prosperity—capital wealth—combined with leisure and ambition [81:6.6]. Scientific knowledge ensures the progress of the material side of civilization [81:6.8], and invention always accelerates worldwide cultural development [81:6.9]. Science guided by wisdom can become man’s great social liberator [81:6.22], and the machine age is not a disaster save to those nations whose intellectual level is too low to discover wise methods and sound techniques for successfully adjusting the sharp losses in employment resulting from the rapid invention of new types of labor-saving machinery [81:6.22].
30.013.p: The spread of civilization must wait upon language [81:6.16], and a living and growing language ensures the expansion of civilized thought and planning [81:6.16], while language differences have always been a great barrier to the extension of peace [81:6.18]. Racial ideals (spiritual idealism) are the energy that elevates and advances human culture from one level to another [81:6.27], and civilization advanced tremendously by the early division of labor and later by specialization, and now depends upon the effective co-ordination of specialists [81:6.29], 81:6.29. The preservation of worldwide civilization depends on man’s learning to live together in peace and brotherhood [81:6.36], and cultural civilization is founded on the intelligent co-operation of citizens and wise, progressive leaders [81:6.37]. Society is a phenomenon of progressive evolution [81:6.39], and the greatest danger to all civilization is the threat of collapse during the transition from established past methods to new, better, but untried procedures of the future [81:6.41].
30.014.h3: 2. Major Facts on the Origin and Evolution of Marriage
30.016.p: Marriage—mate selection—originates in bisexuality [82:0.1]. Marriage is man's reactive adjustment to this bisexuality, and home life is the total of this evolutionary and adaptive adjustment [82:0.1]. Marriage is continuous; it is not inherent in biologic evolution, but since it is the foundation of all social evolution, it is certain to persist in some form [82:0.1]. Marriage gave mankind the home, which is the highest glory of the long evolutionary struggle and the highest civilizing institution [82:0.1], 82:0.2. Mate selection is an inherent predisposition, and marriage is the resultant evolutionary social echo [82:1.2]. Marriage as an institution represents the social evolution of the biologic urge of self-perpetuation, from its earliest form down to the modern era [82:1.8]. Marriage is the mechanism designed by society to regulate and control the diverse human relationships arising from the physical sex differences between men and women [83:1.1]. It functions in two directions: regulating individual sex relations [83:1.2] and regulating lineage, inheritance, succession, and social order [83:1.3], the latter being its older and original function [83:1.3].
30.017.h4: 2) Early Marriage Customs and Sexual Regulation
30.018.p: The evolution of marriage is simply the history of sex control through social, religious, and civil restraints [82:2.1]. Nature cares only for the reproduction of the race, indifferently leaving the resultant problems to society, creating the ever-present major problem of evolving mankind [82:2.1]. Among the early races, there was little regulation of sexual relationships, and because of this sexual freedom, prostitution did not exist [82:2.2]. Marriage evolved from a state of almost complete sexual freedom to the 20th-century standards of comparative complete sexual restriction [82:2.3]. Woman has always been subjected to more restrictive taboos than man [82:2.5]. Primitive marriage did not greatly restrict the sexual freedom of the male, but the wife was required to be faithful to her husband [82:2.5]. Marriage is intrinsically a natural act, and when social evolution reaches the custom-forming stage, marriage appears as an evolving institution [82:3.1]. In early times, the coupled pair spent little time together and rarely ate together, but personal affection among ancient peoples was not strongly connected with sexual attraction, and they chiefly became attached to each other by living and working together [83:1.5], 83:1.5. The approach in primitive marriage was compulsion, not attraction [83:2.2], and before contract marriage, there was marriage by capture [83:2.2]. The shamming of resistance or the pretense of shyness manifested by modern girls regarding marriage are all relics of the old customs [83:2.3].
30.019.h4: 3) Relationship between Property Customs and Marriage
30.020.p: Marriage has always been closely linked with property and religion [82:4.1]. Property acted as the stabilizer of marriage, and religion moralized it [82:4.1]. In primitive society, marriage was an investment and an economic speculation, more a matter of business than of romance, and was planned and decided upon by the parents and elders for the interests and welfare of the group [82:4.2]. The purchase price of the wife was regarded as a sort of forfeit or bond which the husband would lose upon divorce or desertion [83:3.1]. After the bride’s purchase price was paid, many tribes permitted the husband to brand her with his mark [83:3.1]. As civilization advanced, adultery was recognized as a form of theft, involving the violation of the husband’s property rights [82:4.3].
30.021.p: Woman started as the property of her father, who transferred ownership to her husband [82:4.3]. Chastity taboos began as a phase of property custom and were first applied only to married women, not to unmarried females [82:4.5]. Later, chastity was demanded more by the father than by the suitor, because a virgin was a commercial asset to her father and brought a higher price [82:4.5]. During the transition from marriage by purchase to the dowry system, if the wife had been purchased, the children belonged to the father; otherwise, the children belonged to the wife’s family [83:3.4].
30.022.h4: 4) Transition from Matriarchal to Patriarchal Family
30.023.p: Primitive man, not understanding the association between sexual intercourse and subsequent childbirth, believed babies were manufactured in the ghost world [84:1.3], and pregnancy was thought to result from the woman being entered by a ghost, an evolving spirit [84:1.3]. The home was assured by the fact that the reproductive function involves the mother-child relationship [84:1.6]. Mother love is instinctive and did not originate in social custom like marriage [84:1.6]. While the mother-child relationship was neither marriage nor a home, it became the nucleus of both [84:1.8]. The primitive family, developing from the instinctive and biological mother-child kinship, was necessarily matriarchal [84:2.2], which was the only point of transit from the stage of group marriage to the patriarchal family of polygamy and monogamy [84:2.2]. The matriarchate was natural and biological, but the patriarchate was social, economic, and political [84:2.2]. The matriarchate rapidly disappeared as the hunter mores vanished and the herding of animals came to control the main food supply [84:2.6]. This gigantic change from the matriarchate to the patriarchate was one of the most radical and complete transitions ever affected by the human race [84:2.7], immediately leading to greater social expression and increased family adventure [84:2.7]. Pastoral life created a new system of mores—patriarchal family life [84:3.1]. The foundation of family unity under pastoral and early agricultural mores was the absolute and arbitrary authority of the father [84:3.1].
30.025.p: In the early history of marriage, a woman could have only one husband at a time, which was the first step away from promiscuity within the horde [83:5.1]. The husband was free to break this temporary relationship, but these loosely regulated relationships were the first step toward living in pairs, away from the communal life of the horde [83:5.1]. The next stage in marriage development was group marriage [83:5.2], which gradually evolved into various forms of polygamy (polygyny and polyandry) among the more advanced tribes [83:5.3]. Generally, even in polygamy, the home was dominated by the first wife, the status companion [83:5.10]. The concubine practice was the first step toward monogamy and away from frank polygamy. The old taboo prohibiting sexual relations with a wife during pregnancy or lactation greatly fostered polygamy, as primitive women aged very early due to frequent childbearing and hard labor [83:5.9]. Monogamy is exclusive [83:6.1]. Early monogamy came about through environmental compulsion—poverty [83:6.2]. Monogamy is cultural and social, artificial and unnatural to evolving man, but it was wholly natural to the pure Nodites and Adamites [83:6.2].
30.026.h4: 6) Ideals and Challenges of Modern Marriage
30.027.p: Marriage was called a sacrament, but for long ages after the priests of the Sethites made it a religious ceremony, marriage remained a purely social and civil institution [83:8.1]. It was unfortunate to regard marriage as made by divine action, as this led to the concept that the marriage status could not be dissolved irrespective of the circumstances or the will of the parties [83:8.4]. Monogamy is the ideal goal of human sex evolution [83:6.6]. Pair marriage fosters the intimate understanding and effective co-operation best for parental happiness, child welfare, and social efficiency.
30.028.p: Marriage, which began in crude compulsion, is gradually evolving into the majestic institution of self-maintenance, self-control, self-expression, and self-perpetuation [83:6.6]. The increasing tendency to divorce in modern Western society is principally due to the high place imagination and fantastic romance hold in the courtship process, complicated by women's greater personal liberty and increased economic freedom [83:7.7]. Insofar as society fails to prepare its youth for marriage, divorce had to function as a social safety valve [83:7.8]. The greatest threat to the marriage institution is the modern pleasure madness—the alarming increase in self-gratification [84:8.1]. If self-gratification results in the collapse of marriage, the corruption of home life, and the destruction of the family, it tears down man's highest evolutionary achievement—the home—which is civilization's sole hope of survival [84:8.6].
31.title: Evolution of the concept of Trinity and Triunity, Triodite
31.001.h3: 1. Major Facts on the Concept of the Trinity on Urantia
31.003.p: The concept of the Trinity in revealed religion should not be confused with the triune beliefs of evolutionary religion [104:0.1]. Triune beliefs arose from various associations, principally because there are three joints in a finger, a three-legged stool is stable, and three supports can sustain a tent, and primitive man often could not count beyond three [104:0.1]. Except for a few natural pairings like past and present, hot and cold, or male and female, human beings generally tend to think in triads: yesterday, today, and tomorrow; sunrise, noon, and sunset; or father, mother, and child [104:0.2]. As a result of these natural associations derived from human experience, the triune concept appeared in religion long before the Deities of the Paradise Trinity, or their representatives, were revealed to humankind [104:0.3]. Later, Persians, Hindus, Greeks, Egyptians, Babylonians, Romans, and Scandinavians all possessed triune gods, but these were still not true Trinities [104:0.3].
31.004.h4: 2) Three Early Trinity Revelations on Urantia
31.005.p: The first Urantia revelation leading to a comprehension of the Paradise Trinity was made about 500,000 years ago by the staff of Prince Caligastia, but this early Trinity concept was lost to the world during the unstable times following the planetary rebellion [104:1.1]. The second teaching of the Trinity was imparted by Adam and Eve in the first and second Gardens of Eden [104:1.2]. This teaching was not entirely lost even 35,000 years later by the time of Machiventa Melchizedek, as the Sethite Trinity concept persisted long in Mesopotamia, Egypt, and especially in India, where it was perpetuated as Agni, the Vedic three-headed god of fire [104:1.2]. The third teaching of the Trinity was presented by Machiventa Melchizedek, and the doctrine was symbolized by three concentric circles worn on the sage of Salem's breast [104:1.3]. Machiventa had great difficulty teaching the Palestinian Bedouins about the Universal Father, the Eternal Son, and the Infinite Spirit [104:1.3]. Most of his pupils conceived of the Trinity as the three Supreme Rulers of Norlatiadek, some understood it as the System Sovereign, the Constellation Father, and the Creative God of the local universe, and very few grasped the Paradise union of the Father, Son, and Spirit [104:1.3].
31.006.h4: 3) Dissemination and Interpretation of Melchizedek’s Doctrine
31.007.p: Through the activities of the Salem missionaries, the Melchizedek teaching of the Trinity slowly diffused throughout Eurasia and North Africa [104:1.4]. In the later Andite and post-Melchizedek eras, the triune concept and the Trinity concept became mixed and fused to an extent that made it often difficult to distinguish the two [104:1.4]. In Hinduism, the Trinity concept took root in the form of existence, intelligence, and joy, later developing into the Indian concept of Brahma, Shiva, and Vishnu [104:1.5]. The earlier Trinity depiction was carried to India by the Sethite priests, and later Trinitarian ideas were imported by Salem missionaries and developed by combining with evolutionary triune concepts by the indigenous intellect of India [104:1.5]. The Buddhist faith developed two doctrines having Trinitarian characteristics: the earlier doctrine, taught by Gautama Siddhartha, was the Teacher, the Law, and the Brotherhood; and the later doctrine, developed by the northern school of Buddhism, embraced the Supreme Lord, the Holy Spirit, and the Incarnate Savior [104:1.6]. These Hindu and Buddhist concepts were actually Trinitarian hypotheses, embodying the idea of three manifestations of one monotheistic Deity, but a true Trinity concept is not a simple aggregation of three independent Deities [104:1.7].
31.008.h4: 4) Conflict with Monotheism and the Christian Trinity
31.009.p: The Hebrews knew of the Trinity through Kenite traditions of Melchizedek’s time, but their zeal for monotheism was so great that the Elohim doctrine nearly vanished from Jewish theology by the time of Jesus, and the Hebrew mind had difficulty reconciling the Trinity concept with the monotheistic faith in the God of Israel [104:1.8]. Moslems likewise did not comprehend the Trinity concept, which is difficult for monotheistic faiths facing polytheism to embrace [104:1.9]. Hebrews and Moslems, possessing great monotheistic faiths, had trouble distinguishing between the polytheism of serving three gods and the Trinity faith of one God existing as a threefold manifestation of divinity and personality [104:1.9]. Jesus taught his apostles the truth of the Paradise Trinity, but they thought he spoke figuratively and symbolically, having been raised in the Hebrew monotheistic faith and finding it difficult to accept any belief that conflicted with the dominant Yahweh concept, and early Christians inherited the Hebrew prejudice against the Trinity concept [104:1.10]. The first Christian Trinity was proclaimed at Antioch, consisting of God, his Word, and his Wisdom [104:1.11]. Paul knew of the Paradise Trinity—Universal Father, Eternal Son, and Infinite Spirit—but he seldom promulgated it, only intermittently mentioning it in his epistles to the nascent churches, and even then, Paul and his fellow apostles confused Jesus, the Creator Son of the local universe, with the Second Person of Paradise, the Eternal Son [104:1.11]. The Trinity concept in Christianity began to receive recognition toward the close of the first century after Christ, consisting of the Universal Father, the Creator Son of Nebadon, and the Local Universe Mother Spirit [104:1.12]. Though the Christian concept of the Trinity was erroneous in fact, it was substantially true in spiritual relationship, suffering only in philosophic meaning and cosmological consequence, as many cosmic thinkers found it hard to believe that the Second Person of the infinite Trinity sojourned on Urantia, a statement which, though spiritually true, is not literally so, because the Michael Creators fully embody the divinity of the Eternal Son but are not absolute Personalities [104:1.13].
31.010.h3: 2. Major Facts on the Theological Nature of the Trinity
31.011.h4: 1) Philosophical Basis for the Unity and Plurality of Deity
31.012.p: Monotheism arose as a philosophical reaction against the contradictions of polytheism, evolving through the organization of a pantheon of gods, then through Hellenic monolatry, and finally by excluding all gods save one of ultimate value [104:2.1]. The Trinity faith arose from the experiential reaction to the impossibility of conceptualizing the unity of a single dehumanized Deity with unrelated cosmic meaning [104:2.2]. Given sufficient time, philosophy tends to abstract the personal qualities of God from the pure monotheistic concept, reducing this unrelated concept of Deity to the status of a pantheistic Absolute [104:2.2]. It has always been difficult to understand the personal character of a God who does not have personal relations with coequal and co-ordinate personal beings, since personality in God requires that such a God exists in relationship with other coequal personal Deities [104:2.2]. Recognition of the Trinity concept enables the human mind to grasp the interrelationship of love and law in the time-space creation [104:2.3]. Spiritual faith provides man insight into God's love, but he discovers that this spiritual faith in no way affects the settled laws of the material universe [104:2.3]. The expanding cosmic horizon demands that man recognize the Paradise Deity as universal law and acknowledge that the Trinity’s sovereignty proceeds from Paradise to rule over the evolving local universes of the Creator Sons and Creative Daughters [104:2.3]. This divine union is fact, reality, and the eternally indivisible Paradise Trinity [104:2.3].
31.013.h4: 2) The Superadditive Function of the Paradise Trinity
31.014.p: The Paradise Trinity is an actual existence, not a Personality, yet it is a true absolute reality compatible with co-existence with the Personalities of the Father, Son, and Spirit [104:2.4]. The Trinity is the superadditive divine reality resulting from the association of the three Paradise Deities [104:2.4]. The attributes, characteristics, and functions of the Trinity are not simply the sum of the attributes of the three Paradise Deities, and its functions are unique, original, and wholly unpredictable from an analysis of the attributes of the Father, Son, and Spirit [104:2.4]. The Deities do not administer justice as Personalities, but they perform this function as the Paradise Trinity, because justice is never a personal act; it is always a collective function [104:2.5]. The conceptual understanding of the Trinity union of the Father, Son, and Spirit prepares the human mind to accept further revelations concerning other threefold associations where the Infinite works out cosmic manifestations in diverse non-Father functions, such as power, energy, causality, potential, and unity [104:2.6].
31.015.h3: 3. Major Facts on Triunities and Cosmic Relationships
31.017.p: While humanity sometimes attempts to grasp the Trinity of three divine Persons, human intelligence must recognize the relationships of all seven Absolutes for consistency [104:3.1]. Not everything pertaining to the Paradise Trinity pertains to the Triunity; a Triunity is distinct from the Trinity [104:3.1]. Though Triunities may resemble the Trinity in function, they are not intrinsically homogeneous with it [104:3.1]. The whole of reality (Infinity) is presented as existing in the Universal Father, the Eternal Son, the Infinite Spirit, the Isle of Paradise, the Deity Absolute, the Universal Absolute, and the Unqualified Absolute [104:3.5]–104:3.12. The triunity of absolute relationships appears to be indispensable [104:3.14]. The Paradise Trinity is not a Triunity; it is not a functional unity, but rather the indivisible and inseparable Deity [104:3.15]. The Father, Son, and Spirit maintain personal relations with the Paradise Trinity because the Trinity is their indivisible Deity [104:3.15]. Triunities are not substantial, are functional rather than organic, and are associations where the constituents are partners, not co-workers [104:3.16]. There are several existential Triunities, but only one existential Trinity [104:3.16].
31.018.h4: 2) Functional Unity of the Seven Absolutes and the Trinities
31.019.p: In these writings, total reality (infinity) has been presented as existential in seven Absolutes: the Universal Father, the Eternal Son, the Infinite Spirit, the Isle of Paradise, the Deity Absolute, the Universal Absolute, and the Unqualified Absolute [104:3.5]–12. While reason demands a monotonic unity of cosmic reality, finite experience must postulate plurality among the Absolutes and coordination in their cosmic relationships [104:3.4], and a trinity of absolute relationships appears to be inevitable [104:3.14]. Trinities are the functional balance wheels of infinity and the integrators of the uniqueness of the seven infinite Absolutes [104:4.46]. The Universal Father is the primal member of all trinities; he is the personal cause of the Absolutes and the Absolute of absolutes [104:4.1].
31.021.p: The Universal Father is the originating constituent of all seven Triunities [104:4.1]. He is the absolute center, original cause, universal controller, infinite energy donor, primal unity, first divine Personality, and the personal cause of the Absolute [104:4.1]. Triunities are the functional balance wheels of infinity, integrating the uniqueness of the seven infinite Absolutes [104:4.46]. Through them, the Universal Father exercises immediate and personal control over the master functions of infinity [104:3.18]. The seven master Triunities are:
31.022.p: A. The First Triunity — The Personal-Purpose Triunity: Grouping the three divine Persons: Universal Father, Eternal Son, and Infinite Spirit [104:4.3]~6. It is the triune association of love, mercy, and ministry [104:4.7].
31.023.p: B. The Second Triunity — The Power-Pattern Triunity: Consists of the Father-Son, the Isle of Paradise, and the Conjoint Actor [104:4.10]~12. The physical pattern or cosmic constitution of all material organization derives from its function [104:4.9].
31.024.p: C. The Third Triunity — The Spiritual-Evolutionary Triunity: Composed of the Universal Father, the Son-Spirit, and the Deity Absolute [104:4.16]~19. All spiritual expression begins and ends in this union [104:4.15].
31.025.p: D. The Fourth Triunity — The Triunity of Energy Infinity: Consists of the Father-Spirit, the Isle of Paradise, and the Unqualified Absolute [104:4.22]~24. The beginning and end of all energy reality eternally exist within this group [104:4.26].
31.026.p: E. The Fifth Triunity — The Triunity of Reactive Infinity: Composed of the Universal Father, the Universal Absolute, and the Unqualified Absolute [104:4.29]~32. This association eternally confirms the functional infinity realization of everything realizable within the domain of non-Deity reality [104:4.33].
31.027.p: F. The Sixth Triunity — The Triunity of Cosmic Associated Deity: Consists of the Universal Father, the Deity Absolute, and the Universal Absolute [104:4.34]~37. It is the union of Deity in the cosmos, representing the combination of divine immanence and divine transcendence [104:4.38].
31.028.p: G. The Seventh Triunity — The Triunity of Unqualified Unity: Composed of the Universal Father, the Conjoint Actor, and the Universal Absolute [104:4.39]~42. This is the unity of infinity, functionally manifest in time and eternity [104:4.39].
31.030.p: Other triple associations exist not composed of the Father, which are not genuine Triunities but are distinct from the Father Triunities; these are sometimes called Triodities [104:5.1]. Two such associations are: the Triodity of Actuality (Eternal Son, Isle of Paradise, and Conjoint Actor) [104:5.2]~6, which results in the co-ordination of the total realized reality—spiritual, cosmic, or mind [104:5.6], and the Triodity of Potentiality (Deity Absolute, Universal Absolute, and Unqualified Absolute) [104:5.7]~11, which interrelates the infinity reserves of all potential energy reality [104:5.11]. While the Triunities are chiefly concerned with the functional integration of infinity, the Triodities are related to the cosmic emergence of the experiential Deities—Supreme, Ultimate, and Absolute [104:5.12].
32.title: The Seraphic planetary Government and Guardians of Destiny
32.002.h4: 1) Unique Background and Governance Structure of Urantia's Administration
32.003.p: The rule of Urantia is administered by the Most Highs through various celestial forces and agencies, but chiefly through the ministry of the Seraphim [114:0.1]. The planetary government of Urantia is unlike any other world in the system of Satania or even Nebadon, due to several unusual circumstances [114:0.4]. These unique factors include the life modification status of Urantia, the Lucifer rebellion, the Adamic failure, the fact that Urantia was one of the bestowal worlds of the Universe Sovereign Michael, the special role of the twenty-four planetary supervisors, the location of the archangels' circuit, and the recent designation of Machiventa Melchizedek as Vicegerent Planetary Sovereign [114:0.5]~11. Michael is the Planetary Sovereign of Urantia, but he has taken no steps toward the personal rule of the planet, instead establishing the Jerusem commission of twenty-four former Urantia mortals empowered to rule in his stead [114:1.8]. One member of this commission currently resides on Urantia and acts as the Governor General [114:1.1].
32.004.h4: 2) Role and Authority of the Resident Governor General
32.005.p: Every one hundred years of Urantia time, the Jerusem commission of twenty-four planetary supervisors designates one of their number to reside on Urantia and act as their executive representative, the Resident Governor General [114:3.1]. While this narrative was being prepared, the nineteenth Resident Governor General retired, and the twentieth was commissioned [114:2.9]. The Resident Governor General exercises virtually no personal authority in the administration of world affairs, except as he represents the twenty-four Jerusem counselors [114:3.2]. He acts as the coordinator of supermortal administration, and he is the respected chief and universally recognized leader of the celestial beings operating on Urantia [114:3.2]. He performs the role of a fatherly counselor rather than a technical ruler [114:3.3], and most matters concerning the Seraphim and the midwayers are determined by him upon mutual agreement [114:5.3]. The immediate administrative cabinet of the Resident Governor General consists of twelve Seraphim, who are the chiefs of the twelve special groups of angels that directly supervise planetary progress and stability [114:5.6].
32.006.h4: 3) Most High Observer and Chief Seraphim of Planetary Supervision
32.007.p: A Vorondadek Son, representing the Most Highs of Edentia, is stationed on Urantia as a resident observer [114:4.1]. He acts as the trustee of planetary sovereignty unless Michael takes direct action [114:4.1]. In times of crisis, this Vorondadek Son of Edentia becomes the actual and sovereign head of the government, with the exception of certain purely spiritual problems [114:4.3]. The Most High Observer is authorized to take charge of the planetary government during a severe planetary crisis, and there is a record of this having occurred thirty-three times in Urantia's history [114:4.4]. The Chief Seraphim of Planetary Supervision function under the direct command of the Resident Governor General, subject to the transcendent control of the Most High Observer [114:6.1]. These twelve corps are composed of the Angels of the Ages, the Angels of Progress, the Custodians of Religion, the Angels of National Life, the Angels of the Races, the Angels of the Future, the Angels of Enlightenment, the Angels of Health, the Home Seraphim, the Angels of Industry, the Angels of Leisure, and the Angels of Supermortal Ministry [114:6.5]~16.
32.008.h4: 4) Mode of Operation and Coordinating Role of the Chief Seraphim Corps
32.009.p: None of these Chief Seraphim Corps exercise direct or arbitrary control in the sphere to which they are assigned [114:6.18]. While they cannot fully control all matters in their realms of activity, they can adjust planetary conditions and correlate situations to favor the activities of the human groups to which they are attached [114:6.18]. They function as adjusters of ideas, focalizers of minds, and promoters of projects [114:6.19]. They frequently act to enhance any higher ideal already appearing in the human intellect, though they cannot inject new, higher concepts into the human mind [114:6.19]. In addition to many active measures, the Chief Seraphim protect planetary progress from crucial dangers by mobilizing, training, and maintaining the Reserve Corps of Destiny [114:6.20]. The chief function of this reserve is to prevent the collapse of evolutionary progress [114:6.20].
32.010.h4: 5) Composition and Secret Training of the Reserve Corps of Destiny
32.011.p: The Reserve Corps of Destiny is composed of living men and women who have entered the special service of the supermortal administration of world affairs [114:7.1]. These mortals are chosen by the spiritual rulers of the realm to assist in the ministry of mercy and wisdom to the children of time in an evolving world [114:7.1]. They are assigned as human liaison and mortal helpers to the celestial groups of appropriate planetary personages as soon as they appear on the temporal stage with sufficient mental capacity, adequate moral status, and essential spirituality [114:7.1]. These mortals are selected because they possess special ability to rehearse secretly the numerous emergency missions that may arise in the conduct of world affairs [114:7.4], or because they are willing to dedicate themselves whole-heartedly to some special purpose without human recognition or reward [114:7.5]. There are twelve Reserve Corps of Destiny on Urantia, corresponding to the Seraphic supervisory groups of the planet [114:7.7]. The combined corps currently consists of 962 individuals [114:7.8]. Except for fewer than twenty contact personages, the members of this unique group are entirely unconscious of their readiness for action in a specific planetary crisis [114:7.8]. These mortal reservists are chosen by their corps and are deeply trained and rehearsed by the combined technique of the Thought Adjuster and the Seraphic guardian [114:7.8].
32.013.h4: 1) Definition and Assignment Changes of Destiny Guardians
32.014.p: The Seraphic Guardians of Destiny are the guardian angels who minister to individual mortals [113:0.1]. These angels have served on Urantia since man first achieved intellect [113:0.2]. The planetary Seraphim are the ministering spirits sent forth to render aid to those who are to survive [113:0.1]. The teaching regarding guardian angels is not a myth; specific human groups actually have personal guardian angels [113:1.1]. Originally, the Seraphim were definitely assigned to individual Urantia races, but since Michael’s bestowal, assignments are determined by the mortal's mind, spirituality, and destiny [113:1.2].
32.015.h4: 2) Conditions for Promotion to Personal Guardian
32.016.p: Seraphim become known as Guardians of Destiny only after the mortal soul has made the final decision to become Godlike, has entered the third circle of human progress, or has been enrolled in one of the destiny reserve corps [113:2.1], 113:1.5. When the mortal mind breaks through the inertia of animal heritage and attains the third intellectual and spiritual circle of human progress, a personal guardian angel (actually a pair of them) is henceforth wholly and exclusively devoted to this ascending mortal [113:1.8]. Only Seraphim of long service and of the more experienced and tested types volunteer for assignment as Destiny Guardians, and many have gained valuable practical experience on other worlds [113:2.3], 113:2.4.
32.017.h4: 3) Group Service and the Activity of Seraphic Pairs
32.018.p: In ministering to normal beings, the Seraphim are assigned collectively according to the degree of intellectual and spiritual circle attainment of the human [113:1.6]. For instance, humans in the seventh circle are ministered to by one guardian angel and one company of Cherubim who supervise one thousand mortals [113:1.7]. Upon reaching the fourth circle, mortals are grouped ten at a time, and one pair of Seraphim is made responsible for them, aided by one company of Cherubim [113:1.7]. Seraphim generally serve in pairs [113:2.8]. They can act as individuals in virtually all contacts with humans [113:2.8]. When a Seraphic pair accepts a guardianship, they serve until the mortal life is finished, and one of the pair becomes the recorder of the assignment [113:2.9].
32.019.h4: 4) Role as Coordinator with Other Spiritual Influences
32.020.p: One of the most important things a Destiny Guardian does for the mortal subject is to personally coordinate the numerous impersonal spiritual influences indwelling, surrounding, and impinging upon the mind and soul of the evolving material creature [113:3.1]. The Seraphic guardian can and does coordinate the various workings and influences of the Infinite Spirit, ranging from the physical controllers and the adjutant mind-spirits up to the Holy Spirit of the Divine Minister and the omnipresent spiritual presence of the Third Source and Center [113:3.2]. After integrating and personalizing the vast ministry of the Infinite Spirit, the Seraphim begin to coordinate this integrated influence of the conjoint Actor with the spiritual presences of the Father and the Son [113:3.2], 113:3.3. On the spiritual level, the Seraphim are the adjusters who personalize many of the impersonal and nonpersonal ministries of the universe, and on the intellectual level, they are the interpreters who coordinate mind and morontia [113:3.5].
32.021.h4: 5) Principle of Non-Interference with Mortal Will
32.022.p: Angels do not infringe upon the sanctity of the human mind, nor do they manipulate the will of the mortal or interfere with the free action of human will [113:5.1]. They are not supervisors or rulers, but simply guardians [113:5.4]. Their intelligence is not made directly available to the mortal during the life in the flesh [113:5.4]. These angels execute the commands of their superiors, and thus they function independent of the mortal's momentary whims or requests [113:5.3]. They intervene in the scenes of the human drama only in times of grave emergency, and then usually only upon the direct command of their superiors [113:5.4].
32.023.h4: 6) Custody of the Soul and Record After Mortal Death
32.024.p: When the mortal companion dies, the Guardian of Destiny faithfully conserves all values and realities pertaining to the future existence, including the mind patterns, memory formulas, and the morontia realities of the human soul, except for the identity and personality realities of the continuous existence which are represented by the departing Adjuster [113:6.1]. The instant the spiritual luminosity of the Adjuster's presence vanishes from the human mind, the guardian angel reports directly to the commanding Archangel [113:6.2]. The Seraph then proceeds to the first mansion world to await the reawakening of their former ward [113:6.2]. This guardian Seraph functions as the trustee for the survival values of the sleeping soul, just as the absent Adjuster is the identity of the immortal cosmic being [113:6.5]. In cases of non-surviving personalities, the individual or group guardians answer the roll call of judgment, which is the official recognition of the cessation of creature existence [113:6.8].
32.025.h4: 7) Companionship on the Ascending Journey and the Seraphim's Final Destiny
32.026.p: At the first awakening on the shores of the mansion world in the career of an ascending mortal, the human actually first beholds the angelic companions who have so long loved and faithfully walked with them on earth [113:7.1]. On the morontia spheres, the two guardian Seraphim become the human's open companions [113:7.2]. They aid the mortal in every possible manner to achieve morontia and spiritual status as they progress through the transitional world life [113:7.2]. To the Seraphim, the surest way to attain Paradise divinity is the successful conduct of an evolutionary origin soul to the very gates of Paradise [113:7.7]. The Destiny Guardian assignment is therefore the Seraphim's most cherished mission [113:7.7]. Only Destiny Guardians assemble in the initial or mortal corps of the Finality [113:7.8]. These pairs participate in the supreme adventure of achieving spiritual dualization at Seraphington before entering the corps of the Finality, achieving ultimate spiritual unity [113:7.8].
33.title: The Ministering Spirits
33.002.p: Supernaphim are the spirits of service in Paradise and the Central Universe [26:0.1]. They are the highest order of the angelic corps, the lowest group of the offspring of the Infinite Spirit [26:0.1], 26:1.1. Their service is not broadly extended to the major parts of organized inhabited creation [26:0.1]. Supernaphim are restricted to only one phase of action regarding relationship with the Universal Father: "spirit polarity" [26:1.16]. They cannot work alone except when directly utilizing the Father's exclusive circuit [26:1.16]. When energized by the Father's direct ministry, they must voluntarily work in pairs to function [26:1.16]. These brilliant creatures of light are sustained directly by ingesting the spiritual energy of the universe's primary circuits [26:1.17]. They are created in three grand divisions: Primary, Secondary, and Tertiary [26:2.1], 26:2.2.
33.004.p: Primary Supernaphim are the exclusive offspring of the Conjoint Creator [26:2.2] and are created by the Infinite Spirit [26:1.12]. They divide their service equally between specific groups of Paradise citizens and the constantly increasing host of ascending pilgrims [26:2.2]. These angels of the eternal Isle contribute much to the mutual understanding between these two unique classes of cosmic creations [26:2.2]. They are assigned to the command of angelic hosts serving worlds isolated by rebellion [27:0.2]. When a Paradise Son bestows himself upon such a world, completes his mission, ascends to the Universal Father, and returns as the accredited emancipator of that isolated sphere, a Primary Supernaphim is always designated as the chief of assignment for the service spirits on that newly reclaimed sphere [27:0.2]. An ascending pilgrim does not come under the direct influence of these Supernaphim until he actually attains Paradise residential status [27:0.11]. The pilgrims begin Paradise life under the protection of the Rest Stimulators [27:0.10], 27:1.1 and conclude their training season with the Worship Directors [27:0.11].
33.005.p: A. Rest Stimulators: They are the censors of Paradise who proceed from the central Isle to the inner circuit of Havona [27:1.1], cooperating with their secondary complement, the Rest Regulators [27:1.1]. They are the last teachers preparing the pilgrims of time for eternity [27:1.1]. They begin their work on the final attainment circle of the Central Universe and continue until the pilgrim awakens from the last transit sleep, the sleep that graduates a creature of space into the realms of eternity [27:1.1].
33.006.p: B. Dispatch Chiefs: A group sometimes designated as the "Original Pattern Angels" [27:2.1]. They are appointed to preside over the organization of all three orders of these angels: Primary, Secondary, and Tertiary [27:2.1]. They are much associated with the glorified mortal residents of Paradise just prior to entering the Corps of the Finality [27:2.2], and ascending mortals, when taking leisure, tend to cultivate acquaintance with the reserve corps of the angelic dispatch chiefs [27:2.2].
33.007.p: C. Ethical Interpreters: Ethical recognition is simply the individual's recognition of the inherent right of every other individual existence [27:3.1]. They render invaluable assistance in helping Paradise arrivals adapt to the countless groups of marvelous beings encountered during the period from the attainment of residential status to formal entry into the Corps of the Mortal Finality [27:3.3].
33.008.p: D. Conduct Directors: They instruct the new members of Paradise society concerning the perfect conduct of the high beings dwelling on the central Isle of light and life [27:4.1]. They guide the pilgrims, enabling them to avoid confusion and uncertainty that might otherwise ensue [27:4.3]. They primarily function as glorified teachers and guides, concerned with instructing new residents about the nearly endless new situations and unfamiliar usages [27:4.4].
33.009.p: E. Knowledge Custodians: Supernaphim Knowledge Custodians are the higher "living epistles" known and read by all who dwell on Paradise [27:5.1]. They are the divine records of truth, the living books of actual knowledge [27:5.1]. They conduct informal educational courses for the residents of the eternal Isle [27:5.2], but their chief function is reference and verification [27:5.2]. They are the final living summary of the vast network of recording angels, ranging from the Seraphim and Seconaphim of the local and superuniverses up to the Supreme Recorders [27:5.3]. They have classified universe knowledge into seven grand divisions [27:5.5].
33.010.p: F. Masters of Philosophy: These are the "wise men of heaven" [27:6.2], beings of wisdom who utilize the truth of knowledge and the facts of experience in the attempt to master the unknown [27:6.2]. They conduct elaborate courses in 70 functional divisions of wisdom on the southern extremity of the vast Paradise domain [27:6.3]. They derive their supreme pleasure from imparting their interpretation of the universe of universes to the beings ascending from the space worlds [27:6.5].
33.011.p: G. Worship Directors: Worship is the supreme privilege and the first duty of all created intelligences [27:7.1]. They are a special corps of Primary Supernaphim under whose direction the periodic and spontaneous massing of supreme adoration and spiritual praise is conducted [27:7.3]. They teach ascending creatures how to give full and satisfactory expression to their intelligent gratitude and rising tide of appreciation [27:7.4], opening up new and hitherto unknown avenues of expression [27:7.4].
33.013.p: Secondary Supernaphim supervise the work of ascending beings on the seven circuits of Havona [26:2.4]. There are seven orders of these high angels, each having its origin and nature determined by one of the Seven Master Spirits [26:2.5]. They function chiefly in the Central Universe and the seven divine circuits [26:2.5]. They are the servers of the seven planetary circuits of the Central Universe [26:4.1]. About half the total corps is assigned to the instruction of the eternal Paradise pilgrims [26:4.1]. Pilgrims of space are always instructed by Secondary Supernaphim derived from the Master Spirit who sponsors that pilgrim's superuniverse of origin [26:4.10].
33.014.p: A. Pilgrim Helpers: The first of the seven groups of Secondary Supernaphim encountered [26:5.1]. They are beings of quick grasp and broad sympathy who welcome the ascenders arriving in the settled economy of the Central Universe after their long journey [26:5.1]. They function on the seventh circle of Havona worlds [26:5.2], performing their work for ascending mortals in three major departments: supreme understanding of the Paradise Trinity, spiritual comprehension of the Father-Son partnership, and intellectual recognition of the Infinite Spirit [26:5.2].
33.015.p: B. Supreme Guides: Ascending mortals are designated as "spiritual graduates" when they transfer from the seventh to the sixth circle and are placed under the direct supervision of the Supreme Guides [26:6.1]. They function only on the sixth circle of the Central Universe [26:6.1]. It is on this Havona circuit that ascenders gain a new consciousness of the Supreme Deity [26:6.2].
